request:
# Publish partial work as a draft PR, and refuse workflow-file changes

One part of the GitHub Actions workflow work. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below. Don't assume access to any other issue or to `docs/specs/github-actions-workflow.md`.

**Order:** builds on `jig github implement`, which already opens a ready PR for a completed run and comments when nothing changed.

## What

When a run started from an issue cannot finish but did produce changes, jig opens a **draft** PR. One PR comment lists what is still open: the reviewer's unresolved findings, final-check gaps and verification failures. If the run's changes touch anything under `.github/workflows/`, jig publishes nothing and explains on the issue that this automation cannot change workflows.

## Why

Attempts cost time and money. A run that ran out of attempts often leaves useful work and the exact list of what is wrong; throwing both away means a person starts from zero. Workflow files decide what runs with the repository's credentials, so the automation must never ship changes to them.

## Context

jig is a Node CLI (TypeScript, Vitest) that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has one agent implement and another review each slice inside a Docker sandbox, and lands them on one run branch, `jig/run/<id>`. Before editing, read `README.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `CLAUDE.md`, and every `.claude/rules/` file that covers a file you will change, specs included.

The layering is domain rules (`src/domain/`) → flows and steps (`src/flow/`, `src/steps/`) → ports (`src/ports/`) → adapters (`src/adapters/`). Composition lives in `src/app/` and commands in `src/cli/`. Specs sit beside the code as `*.spec.ts` and pass fakes for ports, never module mocks. Anything that touches git is tested against a real temporary repository (`tests/support/temp-repo.ts`).

This issue is one part of the GitHub Actions workflow. In that workflow an operator marks GitHub issues ready, and jig, running in GitHub Actions under a GitHub App identity, implements them, opens PRs and works on review feedback. The jig core, called the *execution engine* (plan, implement, verify, review), stays independent of GitHub. The GitHub code is an *integration*: optional, jig-owned code in its own directory (`src/integrations/github/` unless one already exists). It depends on core contracts, and the core never imports it. jig must start without the integration or its credentials.

- `jig github implement --issue <n>` exists, with its GitHub port, orchestration state ref and publication receipts.
- Run state records why a run stopped: which cap was hit, on which slice, after how many attempts (`src/domain/run-state.ts`, `result.json`).
- Review feedback is free text today (`src/steps/slice.ts`); final-check results live in `src/domain/final-check.ts`.

## Target

- An outcome of `stuck` with commits on the run branch beyond the starting commit opens a draft PR (same head, base and body rules as a ready PR) plus one PR-level comment with the remaining findings, final-check gaps and the last verification failure.
- Findings are published **at PR level only**. Keep any file and line a finding mentions as text, and never invent an inline anchor. Inline placement is a later issue.
- Before any publication, check the change set (default branch fork point to run head). Any added, modified or deleted path under `.github/workflows/` means: publish nothing, comment on the issue naming the files, and record the refusal in orchestration state.
- The comment is repeatable without duplicates, through a receipt in orchestration state.

## Don't undo these

- **Agents and project commands run only inside the sandbox.** Never on the runner host, not even "for CI".
- **Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line, the image, or the sandbox.** The App key and the publishing token stay in the host process.
- **The core never imports the GitHub integration.** Dependencies point from the integration toward core contracts.
- **The host publishes, not the sandbox.** Pushes, PRs and comments are made by the GitHub integration in the host process.
- **No automatic merge.** A person merges every PR. `mergeMode` does not apply to runs this automation starts.

## Done when

- [ ] A stuck run with commits opens one draft PR and one findings comment; a rerun adds neither again
- [ ] A stuck run with no commits opens no PR and comments on the issue
- [ ] A run that changes `.github/workflows/ci.yml` publishes nothing and the issue comment names the file
- [ ] `npm run validate` passes from the repository root


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/14

context.repoSummary: The GitHub integration already lives in src/integrations/github/, separate from core. implement-issue.ts snapshots issues, invokes runJig with merge:false and required git-remote persistence, then publishes ready PRs only for completed outcomes with changes; other outcomes receive issue comments. publicationFor fixes head/base/body rules, and GithubPort already supports draft PRs and issue-style comments. README describes drafts, but implementation does not yet support them. orchestration-state.ts stores accepted requests, PR receipts and comment receipts keyed by runId/outcome/revision; OrchestrationStore persists these in refs/jig/_orchestration with leased updates. Extend this model for findings comments and workflow refusals, ensuring a saved PR receipt does not prevent retrying a failed findings comment. src/domain/slice.ts retains lastFeedback, feedbackHistory, failure counters and failedVerification metadata; src/steps/slice.ts produces free-text review and verification feedback. src/domain/run-state.ts derives stop reasons; src/domain/final-check.ts exposes gaps and unresolvedFindings, but persisted final-check results omit verification output. Preserve file/line references as plain PR-level text. src/adapters/git/repository.ts currently detects net changes using git diff base...branch, which differs from checking commits beyond the starting commit and does not return changed paths. Workflow refusal needs added/modified/deleted paths from the default-branch fork point. Critically, GitRemoteRunStore.save already pushes the run branch during execution, before implementIssue decides publication; inspect this boundary when enforcing refusal before publishing changes. Preserve sandbox-only execution, host-only GitHub credentials/publication, integration-to-core dependencies and disabled automatic merging. Existing implement-issue.spec.ts uses FakeGithub, FakeAgentSession and real temporary repositories and covers publication retries, receipts, no-change outcomes and credential isolation. Follow .claude/rules for Result errors, edge parsing, module-owned rules and setup-based tests without module mocks. npm run validate runs build, typecheck, lint, duplication, formatting, coverage and secretlint.

plan.summary: Publish stuck issue runs with commits as draft PRs, attach one retry-safe PR-level findings comment, and refuse publication of changes under .github/workflows/.
plan.approach: Extend the existing GitHub integration while preserving ready-PR head, base and body rules. Determine partial-work eligibility from commits beyond the run's persisted starting revision, independently of the net diff; stuck runs without commits retain the issue-comment path. Collect unresolved reviewer feedback, final-check gaps and the last verification failure through core-owned contracts, preserving file and line references as plain text. Persist missing verification output with backward-compatible schemas, and avoid presenting resolved feedback history as outstanding findings. Extend orchestration state with separate findings-comment receipts and workflow-refusal records keyed to the run and revision. Reusing a PR receipt must still retry a missing findings comment. Before publishing changes, inspect a NUL-delimited path diff from the default-branch merge base to the exact run head, including additions, modifications, deletions and both sides of renames. If any path is under .github/workflows/, record the refusal and post one receipt-protected issue comment naming the paths; create no PR or findings comment and push no run changes. Address the earlier publication boundary explicitly: GitRemoteRunStore.save currently pushes the run branch during execution. Introduce a generic deferred branch-publication mode for integration-started runs, keeping checkpoint persistence separate from publishing code and ensuring checkpoint/load behavior cannot falsely resume against an unavailable branch revision. Only the host integration releases the inspected revision after the workflow check passes. Preserve normal CLI persistence behavior, required remote state storage, leased updates, sandbox-only agents and project commands, host-only GitHub credentials, integration-to-core dependencies and merge:false. Add behavior tests using FakeGithub, FakeAgentSession and real temporary repositories for draft/no-commit outcomes, independent PR/comment retries, persisted diagnostics, legacy state, workflow additions/modifications/deletions/renames, refusal retries, and absence of run-branch pushes before approval by the path check. Update command documentation and run npm run validate from the repository root.
